translation_decisions.structure_graph_page_scope_decision: StructureGraphPage's five section headings (Active/Capped active/Dominant/Regime-level/Candidate alphas) and its overview <dl> stat labels were deliberately left unchanged, per the task's own Section 18 instruction that this page 'must remain useful to technical users' and must not be 'oversimplified into only cards.' The literal raw underscored token 'regime_level' never appears in this page's rendered text either way (only the already-humanized hyphenated 'Regime-level' compound does); 'candidate' appears capitalized as 'Candidate' in a section title. Both are pre-existing, non-raw-token phrasing. This is a considered scope boundary, not an oversight -- documented here rather than left silent.

added.purpose: Single shared, pure, frontend-only formatter (formatActivationLevelForDisplay) centralizing the activation-level translation table -- used by AlphaCard.tsx, ConflictCard.tsx, and StructureGraphPage.tsx so every place a level is rendered as text shows the same product word for the same underlying state. Never mutates a stored/API value.

gitignore_collision_finding.description: The new shared formatter was initially placed at frontend/src/lib/activationLevelDisplay.ts. git status showed nothing for that path -- the repo-root .gitignore has a generic 'lib/' rule (line 18, evidently intended for a Python venv's lib/ directory) that, having no leading slash, also matches frontend/src/lib/ at any depth, silently excluding it from version control.
gitignore_collision_finding.resolution: Renamed the directory to frontend/src/utils/ (confirmed clear of any .gitignore pattern) rather than modifying the shared root .gitignore -- a smaller, fully frontend-scoped fix that avoids touching shared repository configuration.
gitignore_collision_finding.verified_after_fix: git status now correctly shows frontend/src/utils/ as an untracked addition; all imports updated; full test suite (290/290), typecheck, and production build all re-confirmed passing after the move.
